sections.heading: PNG to PDF: When Images Become Documents
paragraphs: PNG is the image format of choice for graphics with transparency, crisp logos and screen captures. But as file storage and sharing move toward documents, you often need those images inside a PDF: [png-to-pdf:converting PNG to PDF] packages them cleanly.
Reports, invoices, certificates, e-books and portfolio pages are the classic end products of such conversion, where a multi-image PDF behaves better than a folder of loose PNGs.
ChooseTools converts PNG to PDF locally in your browser. The images are laid out on full-page PDF sheets at their full resolution, with transparency and colors preserved, no upload required.
The output is a universally readable document that prints, emails and archives exactly like a native PDF.

sections.heading: How to Convert PNG to PDF in a Few Steps
paragraphs: The process is designed for one-click comfort.

Drop one or several PNG images into the upload area. Optionally reorder them for the sequence you want, then click convert. A single PDF downloads, with every image placed at the center of its own page at natural size.
Because everything occurs in the browser, large PNGs and multiples convert instantly and your originals remain on your device untouched.
The whole operation, from drop to download, normally finishes before a typical cloud converter would finish uploading.

sections.heading: Transparency, Colors and Logo Fidelity
paragraphs: PNG's core strength is transparent backgrounds. During conversion the transparency is respected: no checkerboard artifacts, no harsh white boxes around logos.
Colors render exactly as designed, which matters for brand identity, product images and interface mockups being handed to developers.
Scaled onto the page without resampling, the embedded graphics keep their crisp edges — the PDF reads as professional as the original artwork.
For cut-out product shots and signature stamps, clean transparency means the final PDF looks finished rather than pasted-in.

sections.heading: Multiple PNGs Become One Neat Multi-Page PDF
paragraphs: Combine a whole set of images — interface screenshots, product shots, slides — into one multi-page document that emails and prints as a single file.
Order the pages exactly the way your audience should see them using the item list, and the assembled PDF will be ready to distribute or archive.
For even richer documents, [merge-pdf:merge] the result with other PDF content, or follow with [compress-pdf:compression] if the combined file grows large.
A single multi-page file also survives inboxes and portals far more reliably than ten loose attachments.

paragraphs: Designers send mockups and specs as PNG-packaged PDFs so clients open one file instead of an email of images.
Teachers and creators combine lesson slides and screenshots into study PDFs that stay neatly ordered on phones.

In every case, the browser-based conversion keeps original PNGs intact while producing the polished deliverable the audience expects.

faqs.a: Yes. Transparent areas are carried into the PDF faithfully, so logos and cut-out images keep their clean backgrounds without artifacts.

faqs.q: Can I convert several PNGs into a single PDF?
faqs.a: Yes. Add multiple PNGs and each becomes a page in one output PDF, ordered exactly as you arranged them.

faqs.q: Is the PNG to PDF tool really free and private?

faqs.q: Will my images lose resolution in the PDF?
